A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same STM research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison; relocated and renumbered material can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning experiments, benchmark scores, token-filtering analyses, correctness experiments, and LoRA weight analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds masking controls, model and adapter evaluations, regularization comparisons, and sequential fine-tuning results.

M1.justification: STM still masks high-perplexity tokens using scores from the initial instruction-tuned model. Self-Output, Rephrase, DPF, and STM+DPF procedures are retained. The additional fine-tuning configurations evaluate the existing masking mechanism.

E1.justification: MBPP, MATH, GSM8K, ARC-Challenge, and BIRD retain their training and evaluation roles. v2 Section 5.5 adds a distinct continual-learning scenario involving sequential MATH-to-MBPP training; no new benchmark dataset is introduced.

E2.justification: v2 adds random and low-perplexity masking controls, full-weight and DoRA comparisons with and without STM, and KL regularization. The regularization comparison changes from Self-Output/base-model versus dropout and weight decay in v1 Table 6 to STM versus explicit regularization configurations in v2 Table 8.

E3.justification: v2 introduces normalized task improvement and backward-transfer metrics, additional model configurations including fine-tuned Gemma 9B and OLMo 2, full-weight/DoRA evaluations, controlled masking experiments, and sequential training. Regularization controls are also selected using update norms. The original MBPP 374/90/378 split and individual benchmark metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test high versus random/low-perplexity masking, generator perplexity versus forgetting, regularization with similar update norms, and robustness across adapters and sequential training. Conversely, v1's Llama correctness-rate experiment and Table 5 disappear. The Gemma correctness study and most existing threshold, token-category, and rank analyses remain.

E5.justification: Table 1's descriptive perplexity variances are unchanged, and existing loss-plot variability displays remain. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence-interval procedures, or significance tests; v2 introduces no identifiable new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds results for the new controls, models, adapters, sequential training, and preparation costs, plus Gemma DPF/STM+DPF rows in Table 15. Most raw benchmark scores survive, but Gemma 2B STM's MBPP score changes from 0.4921 to 0.5106 between v1 Table 8 and v2 Table 10. Llama correctness results are removed, and new TI/BWT summaries contain unresolved discrepancies with retained scores.

T1.justification: v2 adds normalized TI/BWT definitions. Its printed perplexity expression changes from exp(...) in v1 Equation 1 to -exp(...) in v2 Equation 3, making the expression negative. Appendix H also relabels the retained summed negative log-likelihood as token perplexity instead of surprisal. The LoRA/SVD mathematics otherwise remains substantially unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claim that low-perplexity training preserves non-target capabilities is retained. v2 qualifies the 'first mechanistic explanation' framing as an empirical explanation of forgetting and explicitly extends applicability claims across fine-tuning techniques and learning settings.

C2.justification: v2 argues that degradation reflects high-perplexity training beyond overfitting alone, using comparisons with similar update norms. Its new limitations section explicitly identifies untested STM models above 10B, missing safety and instruction-following evaluations, and uncertainty about increasing task difficulty. These materially qualify the paper's applicability.

D1.justification: v2 provides additional preparation timings and selected regularization hyperparameters, while retaining hardware descriptions and evaluation prompts. Exact model repository identifiers are shortened. A new public code/data statement supplies only a placeholder repository address, so usable resource availability is not established.

R1.justification: Six references are added, covering perplexity-based pruning, LoRA and forgetting, self-synthesized rehearsal, OLMo 2, and KL regularization. The existing related-work framework remains, with refined emphasis on empirical forgetting mitigation and efficient fine-tuning.

P1.justification: The title, introduction, contribution narrative, method explanation, discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Terminology shifts from in-domain/OOD to target/non-target tasks, Sections 3 and 5–6 are reorganized, appendices are rearranged, and a limitations section is added. The author list also changes.

P2.justification: Main comparison tables are redesigned around TI/BWT and costs, with new experimental tables and a perplexity/BWT scatterplot. Perplexity and Gemma threshold panels are rearranged, and Llama convergence panels are restyled and reordered. Many original displays are retained elsewhere, including v1 Figure 3 as v2 Figure 5.

improvement.justification: New masking controls, update-norm comparisons, and explicit limitations strengthen v1's empirical argument. However, v2 introduces unresolved inconsistencies in central summaries: Llama/MBPP Self-Output TI is 1.55% in Table 2, while retained Table 10 scores imply about 4.02%; Table 5 also reverses Table 2's LoRA TI/BWT values. Together with the worsened mathematical definitions, these issues prevent a reliable judgment of the net quality improvement.
